item.title: Microsoft Announces Voluntary Exit Offer for Up to 60,000 Employees, Including AI Teams
item.description:
Microsoft Announces Voluntary Exit Offer for Up to 60,000 Employees, Including AI Teams

Microsoft is extending a voluntary buyout program to as many as 60,000 staff members across the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and India. The offer reaches a broader slice of the company’s roughly 223,000 employees and includes many teams that work on artificial‑intelligence products.

🔍 Overview

  • Voluntary exit offers are being made to up to 60,000 employees.
  • The program is intended to allow staff to leave with “financial support and career planning resources” while the company trims headcount without another round of layoffs.
  • The offer is described as “new for us” by Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Eligibility covers a wide range of groups, including:
    • AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance, and human‑resources teams.
    • Cloud + AI, MicrosoftAI, and corporate, external, and legal‑affairs teams (partial participation).
  • Teams not participating:
    • Marketing, commercial business, discovery and quantum, and security teams.
  • The offer is not based on age, length of service, or performance, according to an internal HR note.
  • It differs from an earlier voluntary‑retirement program that was limited to about 9,000 U.S. employees meeting a combined age‑and‑service threshold of 70.
Team Group Participation Status
AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance, HR Eligible (full)
Cloud + AI, MicrosoftAI, corporate, external, legal affairs Eligible (partial)
Marketing, commercial business, discovery & quantum, security Not eligible

💡 Why It Matters

  • The voluntary exit offer follows a layoff of 4,800 employees earlier in the year, primarily affecting Xbox and commercial‑sales staff.
  • Microsoft’s leadership frames the program as a way to “help people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.”
  • The company states it may consider future voluntary exit offers “where there is a business and workforce need.”

📢 Official Statements

  • Amy Coleman wrote, “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.”
  • An internal HR note confirms the offer “isn’t based on age, length of service, or performance.”

📅 Recent Context

  • The voluntary exit program arrives months after the 4,800‑person layoff.
  • Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is reported to be planning new rounds of layoffs.
  • The new offer does not target Microsoft’s commercial‑sales teams, distinguishing it from the earlier retirement program.

#Microsoft #Workforce #AI

Source: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees

item.title: Businesses Rehire Staff After AI Fails to Replace Human Skills
item.description:
Businesses Rehire Staff After AI Fails to Replace Human Skills

A growing number of companies are reversing AI-driven redundancies after discovering that human skills remain irreplaceable in key areas.

🔍 Overview

Business leaders are backtracking on job cuts attributed to AI, with many rehiring staff after realizing the technology could not fully replicate human capabilities.

⚙️ Key details

  • 39% of business leaders made employees redundant because of AI.
  • Of those, 55% admit they made the wrong decisions about those redundancies.

🏢 Company examples

Company Action Reason
Ford Rehired over 300 engineers AI failed to match their skills and experience
Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) Reversed 45 job cuts Described the cuts as an “error”
IBM Rehired staff after AI handled routine HR requests AI struggled with complex judgment, empathy, and ethical reasoning

📊 Industry outlook

Research from Gartner estimates that by 2027, 50% of companies that attributed headcount reductions to AI will rehire staff to perform similar functions under different job titles.

💡 Why it matters

Unique human skills like critical thinking, creativity, and ethical reasoning cannot yet be replicated by AI.

#AI #jobcuts #rehiring #workforce #automation #skills

Source: AI layoffs reverse giving young workers a new opportunity

item.title: New York Governor Kathy Hochul Addresses AI Impact and Regulation
item.description:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul Addresses AI Impact and Regulation

New York Governor Kathy Hochul has discussed her perspectives on artificial intelligence, focusing on the technology’s ethical direction and its impact on the workforce.

💡 Why it matters

Governor Hochul has expressed the view that AI should be “less evil”. To address the societal effects of the technology, she has established the Future Works Commission. This commission brings in experts from across the country to analyze:

  • The displacement of jobs caused by AI
  • Identifying who is most vulnerable to these changes
  • Methods for training people to overcome obstacles or embrace AI as a possible career

⚙️ Key details

In addition to workforce concerns, the Governor has taken specific regulatory actions regarding AI-related infrastructure:

  • In July, Governor Hochul signed a one-year moratorium on data center construction.

#AI #NewYork #KathyHochul #Workforce

Source: Governor Hochul: AI should be “less evil”
